items.cite: Howard Pollack, *George Gershwin: His Life and Work* (University of California Press, 2007).
items.note: How did the songs, concert works and opera grow out of Gershwin’s working life? A large documentary biography with separate chapters on the major scores and their reception.
How does Gershwin’s musical language work in the Broadway theatre? A compact study in Yale’s Broadway Masters series, useful beside the larger biography.

items.cite: Ira Gershwin, *Lyrics on Several Occasions* (1959; Limelight reprint, 2004).
items.note: How were words fitted to George’s already-composed tunes? Ira explains his craft through lyrics, discarded ideas and the circumstances of particular songs.

items.cite: Richard Crawford, ‘George Gershwin’s “I Got Rhythm” (1930)’, in *The American Musical Landscape: The Business of Musicianship from Billings to Gershwin* (University of California Press, 1993), chapter 7.
items.note: How did one show tune become a jazz standard and the harmonic basis of other compositions? Crawford follows performers and recordings as well as the Gershwins’ original song.
